intro: Everything PrediGol has learned, in one place. Entities are the teams, leagues, referees, coaches, players and markets over time, each with how far to trust it and what it rests on; matches are the ones it looked at, before and after; learning notes are what the AI's daily cycle wrote down; research findings are what the model research concluded. The post-mortem of each selection has a tab of its own. Reading only: nothing here changes a pick, a probability or a model.

entities.help: Confidence is the effective sample over itself plus a constant: 0 with no evidence, one half at a sample that depends on the kind of memory (for example 30 decisions of a team or 20 matches of a referee), never 1. Each piece of evidence loses half its weight after a half-life (90 days for decisions, 180 for a team's figures, 365 for leagues and referees). A team's corners, cards and expected goals are pulled toward the mean of its league the fewer matches the team has; for them the constant is the number of matches the league's mean is worth, measured on the stored matches, so the confidence is exactly the share of the figure that is the team's own and the rest is its league's. These are conventions of the memory, not model parameters, and changing one makes a new version.
entities.legacyNote: A series without confidence was written by an older version of the memory, which did not measure it; the new version starts on 13 Oct 2026 and continues none of them.
entities.figureRaw: own {own}, rivals {opp} per match (no league figure yet)

events.note: What the AI's daily learning cycle wrote down about a match, a pick or an entity. Each note names the version of the rules that wrote it.

research.note: What the model research concluded and when. A topic that is concluded again keeps its earlier findings: the count says how many there have been.
